description.value: The study investigated mentalising ability in music in patients with behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia and healthy control subjects, and examined voxel-based morphometry correlates of mentalising and non-mentalising task performance.

spans.text: Here, we investigated mentalising ability in a cohort of patients with bvFTD using a novel modality: music.

value: we hypothesised that attribution of mental states (but not other kinds of attributions) to musical stimuli would be selectively vulnerable in bvFTD.

We further hypothesised that performance on the mentalising task would correlate with grey matter volume in medial PFC, OFC and anterior temporal regions previously implicated in both ToM and emotion recognition in music, in FTLD and in the healthy brain ( ; , ; ; ; ).
